claims.text: The initial Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy is single-phase BCC.
Asymmetric XRD peaks in the initial alloy indicate micro-segregation between dendritic cores and interdendritic regions.
The room-temperature fracture strain of the initial alloy is significantly below theoretical predictions.
Adding approximately 4 at.% Cr induces a complex multicomponent Laves phase.
The Cr-induced Laves phase has either the C14 or C15 structure.
The Laves phase forms primarily in interdendritic regions.
The Laves phase occupies approximately 4 vol.%.
At approximately 4 vol.%, the Laves phase forms a reticulated, interconnected, or percolating network.
The interconnected Laves-phase network impedes crack extension by deflecting cracks onto a tortuous path along phase boundaries.
Crack propagation along the Laves-phase boundaries produces predominantly intergranular rather than transgranular fracture.
Triple junctions in the Laves network create stress concentrations that promote void nucleation and coalescence at lower strains.
Cr solute in the BCC matrix causes atomic-size-mismatch lattice distortion and lattice-parameter contraction.
Cr-induced lattice distortion increases the Peierls stress and produces solid-solution hardening.
Solid-solution hardening raises yield strength while reducing strain-hardening capacity.
The combined Laves-network and solid-solution effects cause premature failure and a fracture strain that remains low or decreases relative to the Cr-free alloy.
The Cr-free baseline contains no Laves phase and has a higher fracture strain than the Cr-containing alloy.
The BCC lattice parameter must contract by at least 0.05% relative to the Cr-free baseline for the proposed Cr-distortion mechanism to satisfy its boundary condition.
Annealing the Cr-containing alloy at 1000°C for 10 hours will dissolve the Laves phase.
